mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and subsequent monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE < 4%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% YoY signals robust economic demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where HOUST YoY > 10%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% MoM signals a weakening supply side, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO MoM < -2%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and CPIAUCSL YoY is above 3%, the combination signals a potential overheating economy with loose monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: loose monetary policy with inflationary pressure
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 3%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 250,000 jobs MoM signals strong labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where PAYEMS MoM > 250,000.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances with RSAFS increasing over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is declining and unemployment (UNRATE) is rising, it signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO MoM < 0% and UNRATE MoM > 0%.
